gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the MacBook Neo has only one USB-C port that carries video. Apple's spec lists its second USB-C port as USB 2 for charging and data, with no DisplayPort. On a Neo, a two-cable driver-free extender (Trio 3 Pro without its driver, or a dual FOPO on two full-function USB-C cables) cannot get native video to both screens, and the Neo drives one external display in total.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited pages. Macworld's portable-monitor roundup (cited in chat 2) says plain M1/M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo are limited to one monitor and need free software for the Trio 3 Pro. It does not say the Neo has only one video-capable USB-C port. iTechGuides' '15 Best' page (cited in chat 1) gives no Mac display counts. It says only that compatibility 'depends on the Mac's Intel or Apple silicon generation' and that charging-only USB-C cannot drive a monitor. RTINGS' portable list (cited) did not return its article body, so I could not compare against it. No rival gives the per-chip rule in the maker's own words: M1/M2 Air one display, M3 two only with the lid closed, M4 two with the lid open. No rival pairs that rule with Apple's own port spec.
decides: This narrows ChatGPT's 'Trio 3 Pro best overall' pick to Macs with two video-capable ports that can drive two external displays, such as the M5 MacBook Air (two Thunderbolt 4 ports, two external displays per Apple). On a MacBook Neo, or a plain M1/M2 Air, one added screen is the native fit (the Duex DS line, which Mobile Pixels says shows up as an independent display on one cable). Any dual or triple extender there needs Mobile Pixels' driver (Trio) or a DisplayLink-type driver. An M3 Air drives two externals only with its lid closed, which defeats a lid-mounted extender.

findings.label: USB-C ports and what each carries
findings.value: One USB 3 (USB-C) port with charging, DisplayPort and USB 3 (up to 10 Gb/s); one USB 2 (USB-C) port with charging and USB 2 (up to 480 Mb/s) only, no DisplayPort
findings.note: Apple US spec page, Charging and Expansion section. Chip: Apple A18 Pro. Display: 13.0-inch. Only one port can carry native video to an extender.

findings.label: External displays supported
findings.value: One external display, up to 4K at 60 Hz, with the built-in display at full native resolution at the same time; DisplayPort 1.4 (HBR3) on the USB 3 port
findings.note: Apple's External Display Support section. With no driver, a dual extender can extend only one of its screens on this Mac.

findings.label: External displays and video ports
findings.value: Up to two external displays (two at up to 6K 60 Hz or 4K 144 Hz); two Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports plus MagSafe 3
findings.note: Current US MacBook Air spec page (M5). The page does not state lid-open or lid-closed conditions. Two video ports, one per added screen, means the Trio 3 Pro's two-cable driver-free path is available.

findings.label: Native external display count by chip (maker of the extender's own statement)
findings.value: M1 and M2 MacBook Air: one external display natively; M3: two only with the lid closed; M4: two with the lid open
findings.source_title: Why Are My Two Monitors Showing the Same Display? (Mobile Pixels blog, Jime Chen, 2026-04-23)
findings.note: Quoted: 'which support two external displays natively (M4 with lid open; M3 with lid closed)'. A lid-mounted extender needs the lid open, so an M3 Air gets one native added screen.

findings.product: Mobile Pixels Duex DS series (Duex Max DS, Duex Plus DS)
findings.label: Video path
findings.value: Extends the desktop via a single USB-C or USB-A cable and is recognized by the OS as a fully independent display when connected
findings.source_title: Why Are My Two Monitors Showing the Same Display? (Mobile Pixels blog, Jime Chen, 2026-04-23)
findings.note: Mobile Pixels' own wording. One added screen fits within the one-external-display limit of the Neo and the M1/M2 Air.

findings.label: Cables and Mac driver requirement
findings.value: Two USB-C cables included, one per screen; plain (non-Pro/Max) M1 and M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo need Mobile Pixels' free software to run both screens; Macs at or above standard M1/M2/M3 (Pro/Max, M4, M5) run both without it
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Named reviewer. Macworld also says the Trio is 'compatible with 13-inch to 16-inch MacBooks'. Mobile Pixels' fit range in our record is 15–16 inches. These are two different ranges, so name whose range it is.

findings.label: Mac display driver (maker download)
findings.value: macOS installation guide for Trio Series 2nd and 3rd Gen; macOS 14 and later uses driver v4.1.0 (macOS 11–13 v1.0; 10.15 v1.2; 10.9–10.14 v1.1); the page warns not to plug the device in before installing the driver
findings.source_title: Download Drivers - Mobile Pixels (Trio Series Mac display driver)
findings.note: The page does not name which Mac chips need it and states no limits such as protected video or refresh rate.
